findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following were observed during today’s inspection.
1. The stainless steel sheet sealing the edge of the wall behind the hand sink by the drinks station.
2. The tiles placement around the drainage system between the dish area and the cook line were observed broken.
3. caulking on the multi-compartment sink in the produce prep area was observed coming off.
4. The caulking sealing the countertop right of the dish machine was observed coming off the wall.
5. The stainless steel sheets in the utility sink were observed unscrewed and coming off the wall including the caulking.

PIC was made aware. PIC assured inspector that the relevant repairs will be done. Ensure that these areas are sealed appropriately providing smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.

findings.comment: Inspector observed a build up of soil with in the dish machine. PIC was made aware of the soil build up and PIC immediately got it cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces such as the dish machine are monitored and cleaned at a regular frequency.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a few jugs of milk that had been opened a couple days prior without being date marked. Discussed with PIC and PIC wrote the “opened dates” on the jugs and ensured inspector that they will continue to monitor the date marking on food items. PIC ensured inspector that they will inform staff to observe date marking as well. Ensure that food items are clearly date marked if not used within 24 hours.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: THIS IS A REPEAT VIOLATION. Inspector observed a wet mop head and a rag being store on the floor in the mop sink. PIC was shown the wet mop head and rag. PIC removed them and took them away to be stored properly. A warning notice will be sent to facility reminding them that this was observed during the previous routine inspection on 02/05/2025. Ensure that mop is store in a position that allows it to air dry limiting the growth of bacteria cultures.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. 

Throughout the inspection three separate hand washing sink are observed inaccessible for convenient use. One had several pans in front of it. The other two had items in the sinks preventing their use for hand washing. The PIC was shown and moved the items during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are maintained accessible to facilitate hand washing at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Throughout the inspection multiple food contact items were observed still soiled while in storage as ready for use. It appears that they have not been getting effectively cleaned at the dish washing station. The PIC was shown and moved the noted items back to dish for re-cleaning. It is highly suggested that education takes place with the dish washers to ensure that they review dishes prior to moving them to a “ready for use” location.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-703.11(B) Hot Water and Chemical. After being cleaned, equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils shall be sanitized in: (B) Hot water mechanical operations by being cycled through EQUIPMENT that is set up as specified under §§ 4-501.15, 4-501.112, and 4-501.113 and achieving a UTENSIL surface temperature of 71°C (160°F) as measured by an irreversible registering temperature indicator.

The dish machine in the facility could not, after multiple attempts, reach the critical temperature of 160°F at the surface of the dishes. Both inspector maximum registering thermometer and irreversible temperature indicator as well as the facility maximum registering thermometer were used. The PIC called EcoLab for maintenance and they stated that first thing tomorrow maintenance would commence. The three part sink was set up during this inspection with sanitizer. The dish machine can be used to wash and rinse the dishes and the sink used to sanitize. This is a temporary measure and a follow up will be conducted to ensure that the machine is effectively sanitizing again.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

Multiple spray bottles and sani buckets in the facility would not register on either the inspector’s or facility test strips. These items were remade during the inspection to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective levels at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.16 Drying Mops. After use, mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry.

The mops observed in the mop sink are stored with the heads pooled on the floor of the mop sink. The PIC was shown and moved the mops so that the heads would air dry effectively. Ensure that storage is maintained in such a way moving forward.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

Multiple locations throughout the facility are observed with soiled caulking or caulking that is separating and not maintaining an effective seal. The PIC was shown the relevant areas and instructed to repair/replace the caulking prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(A) Designated Areas. (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use TOBACCO PRODUCTS shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination.

Multiple drinks in the facility are observed located mixed in with foods intended for consumers. The items were shown to the PIC as they were found and removed to correct. Ensure that all employee foods/drinks are stored seperately from consumer foods so as to prevent possible cross contamination. The rule of thumb is generally for the employee item to be stored below and/or away from consumer foods.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: It was observed that there were skewers or other items in the handwashing sinks throughout the facility’s kitchen. Ensure that handwashing sinks are ONLY used for the intended purpose of handwashing. Ensure that handwashing sinks are not blocked and remain accessible at all times. CORRECTED- The items were moved out of each handwashing sink. 

 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There was a container of salad mix that was uncovered in the walk-in cooler. Ensure that all food is covered during storage to protect them from cross contamination. CORRECTED- The salad was removed and placed on the cook line for use. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: Wiping cloths were observed to be stored on the cook line in-between uses. Ensure that if wiping cloths are not in use then they are stored in a sanitizer solution. CORRECTED- The PIC moved the wiping cloths into a sanitizer bucket. 

(B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of food debris/soils:

1. REPEAT- The bottom of the fry freezer along the cook-line has food debris and ice buildup.
2. The floor to the left of the ice machine. 

These areas need to be cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris/soil residues and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 

 (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The following maintenance is observed to be needed throughout the facility: 

1. The caulking on the handwashing sinks throughout the facility is either missing or in disrepair. Ensure that these are re-caulked and are made to be smooth and easily cleanable. 
2. The bottom shelf in the walk-in cooler appears to be broken and needs repaired. 
3. The coving to the left of the office door is in need of repair. 
4. REPEAT- The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation taking place coming from the insulation around the pipe connected to the unit. Ensure that the unit is serviced in a manner that prevents the ice accumulation. 

Ensure that these physical facilities are repaired and maintained repaired. 

PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: An employee beverage was observed stored on the surface of the salad prep station. This drink was removed from this location and placed in a designated employee beverage area that does not pose a contamination hazard. Ensure that employee beverages are stored between use in a manner that does not pose a contamination hazard away from food and food prep areas. This is a repeat violation from the 8/21/2023 inspection report and the facility will be receiving a repeat letter documenting the violation. 
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: It was observed that multiple bowls along the cook-line used to serve food items were visibly soiled after being sent through the wash, rinse, sanitize process. These bowls were pulled from service and placed back into the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle. Ensure that service items are fully washed, rinsed, and sanitized before placing them in the ready to use service stations. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The ice scoops at the bar are observed to be stored in direct contact with the side of the liquor bottles in the side tray. This was discussed with the PIC as an improper storage method due to the hand contact with the bottles and then contacting the surface of the scoops. PIC is removing the scoops from this location and will be placing them in a clean and sanitized container for storage ont he side of the ice machine. Ensure these scoops are stored in a manner that does not allow for contamination between use. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: The fry cooler along the cook-line is observed to have water accumulation in the bottom of the cooler. This item was discussed with the PIC to have the cooler serviced or to see if there is a drain line plugged anywhere. Ensure repairs are made to the cooler that prevents the water accumulation from taking place. Ensure that all food items in this area remain inside containers that create a barrier from the water accumulation and that the cooler is properly cleaned and sanitized to remove the current water buildup. This item is a repeat violation from the 8/21/2023 inspection and the facility will receive a repeat letter to document the violation.
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following areas were observed with an accumulation of food debris/soils:
-The bottom of the fry freezer along the cook-line has food debris and ice buildup.
-The walk-in cooler fan cages and ceiling are observed with dust accumulation.
-The shelving above the silverware wrapping station and the adjacent equipment leading up to the ceiling have an accumulation of dust.
-The walk-in cooler under the shelves and against the walls are observed with food debris/liquid buildup.
These areas need to be cleaned to remove the current accumulation of food debris/soil residues and then cleaned at a frequency necessary to maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: The walk-in freezer is observed to have ice accumulation taking place coming from the insulation around the pipe connected to the unit. The insulation appears to have split where the ice is most apparent. Ensure the insulation is repaired and the unit is serviced in a manner that prevents the ice accumulation. Until repairs are made, the facility has placed a metal pan to catch any further ice that accumulates from the unit. Ensure this pan is removed and placed in the wash, rinse, sanitize cycle at the end of each day and then placed back into this location until the ice accumulation is no longer occurring. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: The main entrance floor drain was observed to be slowly draining with a very pungent scent of sewage coming from the drain. Facility is monitoring the drain level throughout the night. A bucket of water was poured down the drain to observe drainage speed which resulted in very slow draining. Facility will be contacting a plumber to have the floor drains serviced. A follow-up will take place either when the manager team contacts the inspector via cell phone (business card left with facility) or on Thursday 9/14/2023.
 5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. 

Inspector observed an employee take a drink of an energy drink and then place the open can on top of the salad prep cooler. Also, two other drinks were observed on food prep surfaces around the kitchen. The drinks were removed to proper storage areas or discarded. Ensure that employees eat and drink in non food areas.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

The inspector observed the hand sink at prep by the dish room to have an empty sanitizer bucket stored in it. The kitchen staff was already preparing food. Do not place items in the hand sink for storage at any time as this blocks the hand sink. The bucket was removed when I returned to the area. Inspector had not mentioned the violation to staff. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Inspector observed the prep cook making kebobs to rinse the top of the scale off in the hand sink. Do not use hand sinks for anything other than hand washing.  The employee was addressed and the scale food surface was sanitized before use. The violation is considered corrected on site.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

The dish machine sanitizing temperature is 154F. The dish machine repair person has been called. Do not use the machine until it has been verified to work. Call the inspector as soon as the machine is working. The dish machine can be used for washing. The three part sink must be used for sanitizing all food contact surfaces.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The low boy under the rib grill stopped working over night. Manager thinks that the plug just stopped working and claims it was plugged into the socket. The food in the cooler was 66F. The food was discarded. See list in voluntary destruction form. The manager went back to see if the cooler is holding temperature. It is holding at 41F at this time. Do not use unit if it is not working.

Also, the cooler under the bar is holding simply juice at 49F. Three 32oz containers other juice were discarded. Do not use the bar cooler for TCS foods. This juice was the only TCS food in the cooler at time of inspection. The facility is using an ice bath at the bar today. The technician will look at this cooler when they look at the dish machine.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Inspector observed a soiled wiping cloth on the drying rack with clean dishes. Also several wet wiping cloths were in the wash section of the 3 part sink. When finished with a cleaning cloth, put it in the laundry or store it in sanitizing solution. Store wiping cloths properly between uses.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Inspector Observed several single use forks at the wait area stored with the handles down in a coffee mug. The forks were discarded. Store single use items properly protected.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The following non-food contact areas are soiled:
1) inside of grill cooler
2) inside of salad prep cooler
3) inside of expo cooler some water in bottom.
4) behind handles of broil cooler. 
Clean these areas more frequently and maintain clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Observed floors in the facility kitchen to have soil. Ensure that floors in the facility are clean all the way back to the walls, especially under equipment.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed Chicken in the middle drawer of the low boy to be 46F. Beef in the right and left side drawers is 43F. There has been a new Low Boy ordered. The facility called and Air Masters arrived to adjust the cooler. The cooler was holding properly by the end of the inspection. The violation is considered corrected at the time of inspection.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.12: Surfaces such as cutting blocks and boards that are subject to scratching and scoring shall be resurfaced if they can no longer be effectively cleaned and SANITIZED, or discarded if they are not capable of being resurfaced. 

Observed several cutting boards in the facility that have scored surfaces and are in need resurfacing or replacing. Replace or resurface the cutting boards at Onion sink, salad, and 2 green hanging clean over 3 part sink.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-501.110: (A) Temperature of the wash solution in spray type warewashers using hot water may not be less than: 165F for stationary rack-single temperature, 150F for stationary rack-dual temperature machine, 160F single tank, conveyor-dual temperature, 150F multitank conveyor-multitemperature. (B) Temperature for wash solution using chemical SANITIZER may not be less than 120F. 

Wash temperature at the dish machine is 140F according to the thermometer on the machine.  Eco Lab is here working on the machine. A spot check will be completed tomorrow to evaluate the ability of the Eco Lab technician to correct the issue. 
The Eco Lab tech switched the machine to chemical sanitizer which is reading at 100ppm of chlorine.  The violation is considered corrected at time of inspection.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed multiple hand sink issues in the kitchen (at various hand sinks):
1. Cutting knife for steaks was in the hand sink within the protein walk-in cooler. Knife was taken to be cleaned. Cease placing items within the hand sink. Hand sink is for hand washing ONLY.
2. One hand sink was out of soap (near dish machine). Soap was provided for Inspector to wash hands.
3. Hand sink in the protein walk-in cooler was out of paper towels. Paper towels were provided upon request.
4. A putty knife was stuck between the edge of the hand sink (interior of hand sink where caulking should be) at the hand sink near the prep line/bread ovens.

Ensure staff is aware to stock hand sinks when items run low or out and to keep hand sinks accessible at all times. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

(REPEAT) Observed the following non-food contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Mildew and mold has grown around the metal dish machine shelves and behind the dish machine (look at the piping) itself - clean the area. 
2. Interior of fryer doors have build-up of oil and grease - doors and inside of equipment.
3. Mild build-up of dust accumulation in the drink walk-in cooler and main walk-in cooler. 
4. Baffles at the cook line (not the protein grill line) are soiled.
5. Areas in need of dusting: air vent above the main prep line, vent of the reach-in cooler (contains onions) across from salad prep table, sign hanging above the main prep line including the hooks to hang sign. 
6. Wall under the hand sink in the protein grill line area needs cleaned of food splash.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure all the mentioned areas are cleaned before next routine inspection. Items #1-3 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 7/27/22.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following physical facility repairs needed to make areas smooth, easily cleanable, non-absorbent:
1. Areas in need of caulking (either re-caulk due to coming away/moldy or needs caulked): 3 compartment sink and dish machine area, shelving at the dish machine, multiple hand sinks (including interior of hand sinks at edging), shelf above plates at prep line. Inspector pointed out areas. Ensure management walks around the kitchen and caulks as needed to have all equipment smooth and easily cleanable to the walls.
2. Ceiling tile above the protein grill line is stained and frayed. Replace the tile.
3. Several areas have wall that has chipped off the wall: under the shelves at the dry storage (see wall connected to the mop sink), by exterior door behind mop sink, by hand sink near the server station area. Repair the walls.
4. The shelf by the small reach-in cooler at the server station area (near the hand sink) has the particle board exposed due to wear. Ensure the shelf does not have exposed particle board and is smooth and easily cleanable. Shelf is green and has condiments.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Items #1 and #2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 7/27/22.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

(REPEAT) Observed the heat at the dish machine (used as a sanitizing agent) to be fluctuating between 152 - 159 degrees F. EcoLab was called during the inspection and the representative repaired the machine. A part is needed to keep the heat regulating correctly. Representative fixed the issue in the short term. Heat was checked - 161 degrees F. Surface temperature should be at least 160 degrees F, but no more than 194 degrees F. Discussed with PIC. EcoLab suggested a more expensive part be ordered to fix the issue long term. The part that needed repaired today was different than the last part that was needed (see last inspection report, heat was low and EcoLab came during that inspection). COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/23/22.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the bottom reach-in cooler at the bar to be maintaining 50 - 52 degrees F. AirMasters was present during the inspection and correcting the issue with the cooler. Only half and half was present in this cooler, mostly alcohol. Half and half was voluntarily discarded. Sliced fruits and juices are kept in this cooler as well when bar is operational. Inspector will follow-up on 7/29/22 regarding air temperature in this cooler. Alcohol is acceptable to keep within this cooler until repaired and cold holding at 41 degrees F or lower.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the bottom reach-in cooler near the hot holding/cold holding server area (dressings, sour cream, butter, etc. in this area) to have a leak - ponding water at the base. Rags are being used to retain water. Ensure this cooler is fixed before next routine inspection. Water should not be ponding within the cooler. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas to be in need of cleaning due to debris, dust, and other residues:
1. Dry storage wall has food splash behind the shelving. Clean the wall.
2. Mildew and mold has grown around the metal dish machine shelves and behind the dish machine itself - wash, rinse, sanitize. 
3. Mild dust build-up on the drink walk-in cooler fans.
4. Interior of fryer doors have build-up on oil and grease - clean - wash, rinse, sanitize.
5. Dust present on the grates of the fans at the reach-in cooler across from the salad prep cooler along prep line (holds onions) and the small reach-in cooler (contains milk) at the server station.

Ensure areas are routinely cleaned - wash, rinse, sanitize. Clean before next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of caulk or re-caulking: 3 compartment sink at the kitchen, shelving at the 3 compartment sink in kitchen, holes in wall within the dry storage area (as well as the shelf in the dry storage area), multiple hand sinks, holes near the protein walk-in cooler door, hot holding prep line tables and warmer. Some areas had moldy caulk and it needs re-caulked, others areas were missing caulk. Inspector walked with PIC during the inspection and pointed out the various areas in need of caulking. Discussed caulking all small holes throughout the kitchen.

Several ceiling tiles are missing and/or fraying (from heat at grill line) and need replaced.

Ensure all areas are smooth and easily cleanable. Complete repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

Observed the heated dish machine to not be dispensing hot water correctly - surface temp of the heat puck was 145 degrees F (maximum registering thermometer). EcoLab was called during the inspection and the technician has to order a permanent part for the heat element to function properly again. Technician could temporarily fix the heated element until the new part comes. Heating element will take a bit to increase hot water temperature. Facility has a maximum registering thermometer. Use triple sink for tonight’s service if the heat has not increased. Inspector is following up tomorrow, 2/24/22.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (A) Areas designated for EMPLOYEES to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that FOOD, EQUIPMENT, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES are protected from contamination. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

Observed cell phone and small speaker on top of the prep table at the prep line. Observed personal drink with the bar juice at the bottom reach-in cooler. Discussed personal storage with PIC. Ensure items are moved away from food-contact surfaces.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed two employee's to wash hands improperly - a barrier must be used to operate faucet handles. Faucet handles will turned off prior to drying hands, then hands dried - cross contamination. Discussed proper hand washing technique with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed a drain catch in dish machine/3 compartment sink area hand sink. Meat debris was in drain catch. Hand sinks should ONLY be used for hand washing only - do not discard leftover food product in sink. Discussed ceasing practice with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed bottom drawer cold holding that contains chicken (in grill area) to not be holding temperature. Multiple probed pieces of chicken in front of drawer and back of drawer all resulted in roughly 52-54 degrees F. All chicken was voluntarily discarded. Discussed monitoring this particular cold holding drawer. PIC will test drawer and repair as needed. Inspector will follow-up on 5/3/21.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

Observed multiple stacks of drying equipment and utensils at the dish machine/3 compartment sink area to be stacked - does not allow for air drying. Cease practice. Discussed with PIC. All washed, rinsed, and sanitized equipment should not be stacked - allow for air drying, then stack.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

Observed multiple stacks of plates at the prep line to have splashed food debris on plates. PIC removed plates and brought to dish area. Discussed not taking plates from the dish area that have caked on food debris and/or ceasing use of plates that have food splatter. COS.
